title: Vote on releasing Apache Iceberg C++ 0.3.0 RC3
summary: Junwang (zhjwpku) proposed release candidate 3 of Apache Iceberg C++ 0.3.0, based on commit 0284683f, with a vote open for at least 72 hours. Voters verified the candidate on macOS, Ubuntu and Debian, mostly with the `verify_rc.sh` script. Gang (wgtmac) noted that REST catalog verification can be skipped with `VERIFY_REST=0` if libcurl causes problems. Matt (zeroshade) hit such a problem on Ubuntu 25.10: the default libcurl package does not install `libcurl.pc`, so CMake could not find the system curl and failed instead of vendoring or fetching it. He said this was not blocking and suggested updating the README and the CMake configuration; Junwang agreed to fall back to a vendored curl when no system installation is found. The vote passed with 3 binding and 10 non-binding +1 votes, and the release manager said he would proceed with the release and write the release blog.

positions.stance: Votes +1 (binding); the build should vendor or fetch libcurl when the system package is not found instead of failing, and the README should say so, but this does not block the release.
Agrees the build should fall back to a vendored curl when no system installation is found and will work on a fix and a README update.

outcome.note: Passed with 3 binding +1 votes and 10 non-binding +1 votes; no -1 or +0 votes were reported.

why_it_matters: Apache Iceberg C++ 0.3.0 was approved for release, with a follow-up to make the build work when the system libcurl development files are missing.
